en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga,
Chapter on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Acelaka-vagga 43.
The Training Rule on Eating Together.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyaputta, having gone to the house of a friend, sat down together with that friend’s wife in the bedchamber.
Then that man approached the Venerable Upananda the Sakyaputta; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyaputta, he sat down to one side.
Sitting to one side, that man said this to his wife: “Give almsfood to the noble sir.”
Then that woman gave almsfood to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan-son.
Then that man said to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan-son, “Go, venerable sir, from where the noble one’s alms have been given.
Then that woman, having observed, “This man is possessed by lust,” said to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan-son, “Sit down, venerable sir; do not go away.”
A second time that man said to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan-son, “Go, venerable sir, where alms have already been given to the master.
A third time that woman said to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan-son, “Sit down, venerable sir; do not go away.”
Then that man went out and complained to the monks:
"Venerable sirs, this noble Upananda was sitting with my wife in the bedchamber.
When I asked him to leave, he did not wish to go."
“We have many duties; we have much to do.
Those monks who were few in desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan-son sit down intruding upon a family that is eating?”... [as before]...
“Is it true, Upananda, that you sit intruding upon a family where a meal is being served?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him … [as before] …
“How, foolish man, can you sit down intruding upon a family that is eating?
This, foolish man, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:”
“Whatever monk, having intruded upon a family where a meal is being served, should sit down, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever monk” means whichever kind of monk... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhu" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
A "family with food" means:
It is when there is both a woman and a man, and both the woman and the man have not departed [from the monastery], and both are not free from lust.
"Having intruded" means having entered [the dwelling].
"She should sit down" means:
if she sits down in a large house having left the reach of hand from the door-joint, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If she sits down in a small house having passed beyond the central pillar, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If, in a sleeping quarters, perceiving it as a sleeping quarters, one takes a seat intruding upon a family that has food, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, in a sleeping quarters, being doubtful about it, one takes a seat intruding upon a family that has food, there is an offense of expiation.
If, in a sleeping quarters, not perceiving it as a sleeping quarters, one takes a seat intruding upon a family that has food, there is an offense of expiation.
If it is not a sleeping chamber and he perceives it as a sleeping chamber, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is not a sleeping chamber and he is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is not a sleeping chamber and he perceives it as not a sleeping chamber, there is no offense.
There is no offense if one sits in a large house without leaving the reach of the hand from the door-frame,
or if one sits in a small house without crossing over the central ridge-pole.
There is a second monk;
both have gone forth,
and both are free from passion.
In a house where a person is sleeping,
in the case of one who is insane,
and for the first offender.
The third training rule concerning eating with a full mouth is finished.
